# Cherry MX Keycap Body Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Replace the placeholder slab with a generated Cherry MX compatible keycap body and a Base Shape choice (Square, Circle, Trace) in the Clicker Maker.

**Architecture:** The body is generated by the shared plain-JS geometry module (`resources/clicker/`), so the browser preview and the Node build produce the same mesh. Square/Circle outlines are analytic; Trace derives its outline from the artwork silhouette on a coarse grid (distance transform, closing, hole fill, dilation, tracing, simplification). Laravel only stores the new `base_shape` setting, seeds the new body and passes the body config through.

**Tech Stack:** Laravel 12, Pest, Vue 3 + TypeScript + Inertia, plain ESM JS tested with `node --test` (`npm run test:clicker`).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-cherry-mx-keycap-body-design.md` (binding; read it first). Base design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-clicker-maker-design.md`.

## Global Constraints

- Geometry code in `resources/clicker/` is plain ESM JavaScript with no browser-only or Node-only APIs (it runs in both); allowed dependencies: earcut, fflate, pngjs (pngjs only in `build.mjs` and tests).
- Units are millimetres. Defaults from the spec: size 30, rim 2, corner_radius 4, height 8, socket_depth 4.5, stem span 4.2, arm 1.35, wall 1.2.
- Every body shell must pass `isClosedManifold` from `resources/clicker/mesh.js`.
- Bodies without `generator` keep their current behaviour unchanged (static STL files, cap mask, grey slab proxy); existing tests must keep passing.
- Money path, locking, queue and sweeper behaviour are not touched.
- Do not name third-party toy or figure brands in UI copy, prompts or file names. Do not copy any third party's geometry or assets.
- Never run `migrate:fresh`, `config:cache` or `db:wipe`; Pest runs only on in-memory SQLite; never print or commit API keys.
- Create and edit files with the Write/Edit tools, not shell heredocs. Run Pint/Prettier only on files you changed.
- Browser checks use a throwaway test user (never the owner's account, user id 5), deleted afterwards with its clickers and files; report every process left running; if a kill or move is denied, report it, do not work around it.
- Commit messages end with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

### Task 1: Raster and polygon primitives

**Files:**
- Create: `resources/clicker/shapes.js`
- Test: `resources/clicker/tests/shapes.test.js`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces (all pure functions, masks are `Uint8Array` of 0/1 with `width`, `height`; distances are in pixels):
  - `distanceToZero(mask, width, height) -> Float32Array`: Euclidean distance from every pixel to the nearest pixel whose mask value is 0 (0 for mask 0 pixels). Exact (Felzenszwalb two-pass squared EDT). A pixel on the image border is treated as having background outside the image only if you pass `outsideIsZero = true` (4th parameter, default false).
  - `dilate(mask, width, height, radius) -> Uint8Array`: disc dilation; a pixel is set when a set pixel exists within `radius` (Euclidean, `<=`). `radius <= 0` returns a copy.
  - `erode(mask, width, height, radius) -> Uint8Array`: disc erosion (set pixels with `distanceToZero > radius`, the outside of the image counts as background).
  - `closeGaps(mask, width, height, radius) -> Uint8Array`: dilate then erode, on a grid the caller has already padded by at least `radius` pixels.
  - `fillHoles(mask, width, height) -> Uint8Array`: sets every background pixel not 4-connected to the image border.
  - `components(mask, width, height) -> {count: number, labels: Int32Array}` (4-connected, labels from 1, 0 for background).
  - `poleOfInaccessibility(mask, width, height) -> {x, y, r}`: pixel centre (x + 0.5, y + 0.5) with the largest `distanceToZero(…, outsideIsZero = true)`, and that distance `r` in pixels; ties resolved by the first in scan order.
  - `convexHull(points) -> [x, y][]` counter-clockwise, no repeated first point (Andrew's monotone chain), `points` is `[x, y][]`.
  - `simplifyRing(ring, tolerance) -> [x, y][]`: Douglas-Peucker on a closed ring (split at the two points farthest apart so the ring is treated as two open paths); never returns fewer than 3 points for a ring that had at least 3 distinct non-collinear points.
  - `crossRing(cx, cy, span, arm) -> [x, y][]`: the 12-point counter-clockwise outline of a plus sign centred on (cx, cy) whose two bars are `span` long and `arm` wide.
  - `ensureCcw(ring) -> ring` (reverses when `signedArea` from `trace.js` is negative).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests** in `shapes.test.js` using `node:test` + `node:assert/strict` (match `tests/raster.test.js`). Cover at least:
  - `distanceToZero` on a 5x5 grid with a single 0 in the corner: diagonal neighbour is sqrt(2), a far pixel matches `Math.hypot`.
  - `dilate`/`erode` of a single pixel and of a 7x7 block by radius 2 (counts: dilated single pixel = 13 pixels for radius 2; eroded 7x7 block by radius 2 leaves the central 3x3 for the disc test `distance > 2`... compute the expectation from the definition, do not guess).
  - `closeGaps` joins two blocks separated by a 2-pixel gap with radius 2 and does not join them with radius 0.
  - `fillHoles` fills a ring but leaves an open "C" shape unchanged.
  - `components` counts 2 for two separated blocks, treats diagonal contact as separate.
  - `poleOfInaccessibility` of a 9x9 filled square inside a 15x15 grid is the centre with `r` 5 (outsideIsZero); of a thick plus sign it is the crossing.
  - `convexHull` of a square with an interior point; `simplifyRing` of a circle of 200 points at tolerance 0.05 keeps the radius within tolerance and has fewer than 200 points; a square with extra collinear points returns exactly 4 points.
  - `crossRing` has 12 points, positive area equal to `2*span*arm - arm*arm`, bounding box `span` x `span`.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run** `node --test resources/clicker/tests/shapes.test.js` and see the failures.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `shapes.js` (import `signedArea` from `./trace.js`). Keep it dependency free.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run** `npm run test:clicker`; everything passes (previous 38 plus the new ones).
- [ ] **Step 5: Commit** `git add resources/clicker/shapes.js resources/clicker/tests/shapes.test.js` with message `feat: raster and polygon primitives for the keycap body`.

### Task 2: Keycap body mesh builder

**Files:**
- Create: `resources/clicker/keycap.js`
- Test: `resources/clicker/tests/keycap.test.js`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `extrudePolygons`, `isClosedManifold`, `meshVolume`, `bounds` from `mesh.js`; `capPolygon` is in `geometry.js` (do not import geometry.js from keycap.js, to avoid a cycle: take the outline ring as an argument); `crossRing`, `ensureCcw`, `simplifyRing` from `shapes.js`.
- Produces:
  - `KEYCAP_DEFAULTS = {size: 30, rim: 2, corner_radius: 4, height: 8, socket_depth: 4.5, stem: {span: 4.2, arm: 1.35, wall: 1.2}}`
  - `keycapConfig(body) -> object`: `body.keycap` merged over `KEYCAP_DEFAULTS` (deep for `stem`).
  - `stemClearance(keycap) -> number`: `(span / 2) * Math.hypot(1, arm / span) + wall` (the minimum distance from the stem centre to the outline).
  - `mergeMeshes(meshes) -> {positions: Float32Array, indices: Uint32Array}`: concatenation with index offsets.
  - `buildKeycapBody({outline, stem, keycap}) -> {kind: 'body', name: 'Body', hex: '#9CA3AF', positions, indices}`: `outline` is a CCW ring in mm, `stem` is `{x, y}`, `keycap` a full config. Shell A = `extrudePolygons([{outer: outline, holes: [crossRing(stem.x, stem.y, span, arm)]}], 0, socket_depth + 0.4)`; shell B = `extrudePolygons([{outer: outline, holes: []}], socket_depth, height)`; merged. (The cross hole is a hole of shell A, which has holes passed as CW rings if `extrudePolygons` requires it: check `mesh.js` and `ensure` the orientation it expects; cover with the manifold test.)
  - `squareOutline(keycap) -> ring` (rounded square, `size`, `corner_radius`, using the same corner-arc approach as `capPolygon` in `geometry.js`, 8 segments per corner) and `circleOutline(keycap) -> ring` (`size` diameter, 72 segments). Both CCW, centred on the origin.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests** in `keycap.test.js`: for square and circle (and a hand-made L-shaped outline with the stem inside the thick part): each shell is closed manifold (rebuild each shell via `extrudePolygons` in the test, or export the two shells from `buildKeycapBody` as `shells` on the return value so the test can check them; do the latter and keep `positions`/`indices` as the merged mesh); merged volume equals shell A volume + shell B volume; shell A volume equals outline area x (socket_depth+0.4) minus cross area x (socket_depth+0.4) within 0.5 percent; the merged bounds span z 0 to `height` and x/y equal the outline bounds; the cross hole is visible: the mesh contains vertices at `stem.x +/- span/2` and `stem.y +/- arm/2`. `squareOutline` area is below `size*size` and above `size*size - (4 - Math.PI) * corner_radius**2 - 0.5`; `circleOutline` area is within 0.5 percent of `Math.PI * (size/2)**2`. `keycapConfig({})` returns the defaults and `keycapConfig({keycap: {stem: {arm: 1.5}}})` keeps the other stem values.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run** `node --test resources/clicker/tests/keycap.test.js`, see failures.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `keycap.js`.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run** `npm run test:clicker`, all pass.
- [ ] **Step 5: Commit** `feat: generated Cherry MX keycap body mesh`.

### Task 3: Trace outline and pipeline integration

**Files:**
- Modify: `resources/clicker/geometry.js`, `resources/clicker/build.mjs` (only if needed)
- Create: `resources/clicker/trace-outline.js`
- Test: `resources/clicker/tests/trace-outline.test.js`, `resources/clicker/tests/keycap-pipeline.test.js`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: everything from Tasks 1 and 2; existing `analyzeArtwork`, `buildParts`, `toMm`, `traceLabel`, `downscale`, `applyCapMask`.
- Produces:
  - `traceOutline({image, frame, keycap}) -> {outline: ring (mm, CCW), stem: {x, y}, stemRadius: number (mm, the clearance at the stem), notes: string[]}` in `trace-outline.js`. `image` is the scaled RGBA image analyzeArtwork already holds; `frame` is `{left, top, mmPerPx}` for it (the artwork's top-left corner in mm and mm per pixel). Steps exactly as in the spec "Trace" section, on a coarse grid of cell size `max(0.08, longestSideMm / 512)` that covers the artwork bounds plus a pad of `rim + 8 mm` on every side (so dilation and closing never clip). The silhouette is sampled at cell centres from the alpha channel. Notes: use the hull fallback message `"The artwork has separate pieces, so the shape joins them with a wrapped outline."` when the hull is used.
  - `analyzeArtwork(image, settings, body, quality)` additions for `body.generator === 'mx_keycap'`: `keycap = keycapConfig(body)`; `shape = settings.base_shape ?? 'square'` (an unknown value is treated as `'square'`). Square/Circle: a `cap` object for the existing mask code (`{shape: 'rounded' | 'circle', width: size, height: size, corner_radius, top_z: height, inset: 0}`) and `artwork_area = {cx: 0, cy: 0, width: size - 2*rim, height: size - 2*rim}`; `analysis.cap = {outline: squareOutline | circleOutline, stem: {x: 0, y: 0}}`. Trace: `artwork_area = {cx: 0, cy: 0, width: size, height: size}`, skip `applyCapMask`, `analysis.cap = {outline, stem}` from `traceOutline`, append its notes. `analysis.blockers` is `[]` unless Trace's `stemRadius` (distance from the pole to the outline in mm) is below `stemClearance(keycap)`, in which case it holds the spec's exact message. For non-generator bodies `analysis.cap` is undefined and `analysis.blockers` is `[]`.
  - `buildParts` for generator bodies: `top = keycap.height`; throws `Error(analysis.blockers[0])` when there are blockers; appends the body part from `buildKeycapBody({outline: analysis.cap.outline, stem: analysis.cap.stem, keycap})` last. Non-generator behaviour unchanged.
  - `build.mjs`: no change expected (it already passes `job.body`, appends `job.bodyFiles` parts); verify a job with a generator body and no `bodyFiles` produces a 3MF whose last object is named `Body`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write failing tests.** `trace-outline.test.js` with synthetic RGBA images built via `makeImage` from `tests/helpers.js` (circle of radius 100 px, a ring of outer radius 100 / inner 70 with a separate dot 40 px away, a thin 4-px-wide 200-px line, two blocks 600 px apart, a fully opaque rectangle, and a soft-edged alpha disc). Assert: outline is CCW, closed, simple enough that `isClosedManifold(extrudePolygons([{outer: outline, holes: []}], 0, 1))` holds; the outline contains every opaque pixel centre (in mm via the frame) with at least `rim - 0.2` mm margin from the artwork edge for the disc; the ring is filled (no holes); ring + dot within 1 mm closes into one component (no hull note) while the two far blocks use the hull and note; the thin line yields `stemRadius` below the clearance (blocker); the disc's stem is at its centre within 0.3 mm. `keycap-pipeline.test.js`: for each of `square`, `circle`, `trace` run `analyzeArtwork` + `buildParts` on `sampleArtwork` from `tests/helpers.js` with a generator body (add `KEYCAP_BODY = {generator: 'mx_keycap', cap: {shape: 'rounded', width: 30, height: 30, corner_radius: 4, top_z: 8, inset: 0}, artwork_area: {cx: 0, cy: 0, width: 26, height: 26}, max_layer_height: 3, min_feature: 0.8, keycap: {}}` to `helpers.js`): parts end with a `body` part, colour parts sit at z >= 8 (check `bounds` min z of each colour part is 8) and inside the body's x/y bounds, blockers empty; a legacy body (`BODY` from helpers) still returns no body part and `analysis.cap` undefined; a thin-line artwork with `base_shape: 'trace'` makes `buildParts` throw the blocker message; `build.mjs` end to end (copy the approach in `tests/build.test.js`) for `trace` with a generator body: exits 0, 3MF has an object named `Body`.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run** `npm run test:clicker`, see the new failures only.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `trace-outline.js` and the `geometry.js` changes. Keep `analyzeArtwork`'s legacy path byte-for-byte equivalent in output (existing tests are the guard).
